questions.text: What must students do before Professor Aidarov's Thursday session?
opts: Write a summary of last week
Submit one indirect question they genuinely want answered
questions.correct: Submit one indirect question they genuinely want answered
questions.hint: "students must submit one question they genuinely want answered — written as a proper indirect question."

questions.text: Kamila says she still asks questions quickly without thinking.
questions.hint: "I used to fire off questions... Now I think before I ask." — she has changed.

questions.text: What does Amir's "garbage in, garbage out" principle mean in this context?
opts: A poor question produces a poor answer
questions.correct: A poor question produces a poor answer
questions.hint: "Garbage in, garbage out... If I ask a poorly structured question, I get a vague answer."

questions.text: What does Rustam say the best question does?
opts: Makes the other person think and opens something up
questions.correct: Makes the other person think and opens something up
questions.hint: "The best question... makes the other person think... actually opens something up."

questions.text: The final paragraph says universities rarely teach students how to ___ .
questions.hint: "Universities teach students what to know. They rarely teach them how to ask."

questions.text: Tag questions signal closed-mindedness and a lack of interest in others' views.
questions.hint: "They signal openness... I want to know what you think too."

questions.text: What topic does Kamila want to specialise in?
questions.hint: "bilingual language acquisition, particularly in early childhood."

questions.text: Kamila's research paper has already been published.
questions.hint: "It hasn't been published yet, but Professor Aidarov has submitted it."

questions.text: Kamila personally conducted ___ parent interviews.
questions.hint: "I personally conducted twelve of the parent interviews."

questions.text: What does Kamila say is the main challenge in bilingual research?
questions.hint: "it's the difficulty of controlling variables."

questions.text: What does Kamila ultimately want to contribute to?
questions.hint: "contribute to educational policy in Kazakhstan."

questions.text: The interview uses which type of questions?
questions.hint: The interviewer says "Could you tell me...?" and "Do you know...?" — all indirect question structures.

questions.text: "Where is the library?" → Indirect: "Could you tell me ___?"
questions.hint: No inversion in indirect: "WHERE THE LIBRARY IS." ✅

questions.text: "What time does it start?" → "Do you know ___?"
questions.hint: Drop "does", normal order: "WHAT TIME IT STARTS." ✅

questions.text: "Is she coming?" → "Do you know ___ she is coming?"
questions.hint: Yes/no question → "whether" or "if". "...WHETHER SHE IS coming." ✅

questions.text: "She's very talented, ___ she?" (tag)
questions.hint: Positive (is) → negative tag (isn't). "She's talented, ISN'T she?" ✅

questions.text: "He doesn't know the answer, ___ he?" (tag)
questions.hint: Negative (doesn't) → positive tag (does). "...doesn't know, DOES he?" ✅

questions.text: "Could you tell me where does she work?" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "Could you tell me WHERE SHE WORKS?" — no inversion in indirect questions!

questions.text: "I am right, ___ ?" — the correct special tag:
questions.hint: "I am" → "AREN'T I?" — special case. "amn't" does not exist in standard English! ✅

questions.text: "Let's go to the library, ___ ?"
questions.hint: "Let's" → "SHALL WE?" — special tag for suggestions. ✅

questions.text: "An indirect question" is:
opts: A question embedded in a polite structure
A question without a question mark
questions.correct: A question embedded in a polite structure
questions.hint: "indirect" = not going straight to the point. Indirect questions use polite frames like "Could you tell me...?"

questions.text: "An abrupt answer" means:
opts: A sudden, not very polite answer
questions.correct: A sudden, not very polite answer
questions.hint: "abrupt" = sudden and not very friendly or polite.

questions.text: A ___ question is added to the end of a statement to check or confirm.
questions.hint: A "tag question" (разделительный вопрос) is a short question added to a statement.

questions.text: "The skill is underrated." "Underrated" means:
opts: Not given enough credit for its value
questions.correct: Not given enough credit for its value
questions.hint: "underrated" = not appreciated or valued as much as it deserves to be.

questions.text: "She needs a more precise question." "Precise" means:
questions.hint: "precise" = exact, accurate, specific. A precise question leaves no room for misunderstanding.
